$schema_note: Tuned numbers for the squad group system. Decisions + rationale live in docs/design/squad-group-system.md. All values are PROTOTYPE DIALS (first pass, not playtested) — same status as economy.json. Per-type stat/formation/growth dials live in unit-types.json, not here.
revision_note: 0.3 is the typed-unit rework, owner ask 2026-07-27: 'retinue turned into simpler units, much like Total War... spearmen and archers.' Squad = unit now (squad-group-system.md §1.0). squad_target_size_formula (0.2, single pool) replaced by squad_manager.typed_allocation (two pools, Spearmen claim first). Adds map_mode (new third view) and army_view_lens_geometry.orthographic_check. view_modes/selection_responsiveness/yaw_envelope carried over from 0.2 unchanged except where noted.

squad_manager.max_squads_note: Fixed through the near-term bigger-retinue stage. Not a power cap (GDD §7 Law 2) — bounds the number of command handles a player juggles, not total retinue power. Matches the muster HUD's existing 4-card-per-wing mirrored layout. Now SHARED across both unit types (typed_allocation below), not per-type.

typed_allocation.formula: WantedUnits(type) = ceil(Pool(type) / squad_size_legibility_ceiling); Units(spearmen) = max(1, WantedUnits(spearmen)) if Pool(spearmen) > 0 else 0; Units(archers) = clamp(max(1, WantedUnits(archers)), 0, max_squads - Units(spearmen)) if Pool(archers) > 0 else 0
typed_allocation.claim_order_note: Spearmen claim their fair share of the 8-handle budget first (CLASSES.md: 'high count, disciplined', the primary identity); Archers get the remainder, folding overflow into their own existing units if the budget runs out before their want is met. Replaces 0.2's single-pool 'ceil(alive_retinue / max_squads)' formula, which assumed one undifferentiated pool.
typed_allocation.recompute_cadence: every formation repack, same as 0.2 — but now TWO independent dense repacks (one per type), see squad-group-system.md §1.2/§8

squad_manager.squad_size_legibility_ceiling_note: Approximate body count past which one unit stops reading as a single commandable shape at a glance (Unit/Squad View target, §4.2/§7 of the spec). Not the same constraint as Army View's lens-geometry ceiling — see army_view_lens_geometry below. Same value, now applied per-type independently.
squad_manager.membership_assignment: assigned once at recruit time (fill-lowest-first within the soldier's type across that type's live units), persists for that soldier's lifetime — TYPE is assigned at the same moment and is equally permanent
squad_manager.membership_assignment_note: MUST NOT be derived from the per-frame dense formation-repack slot index (today's SquadIdForSlot behavior) — see squad-group-system.md §1.3 for why that breaks once units carry independent stances AND types.

army_view.subject: the whole standing retinue, as <= max_squads blocks
army_view.representation: aggregate block per squad — NEVER individual per-soldier billboards
army_view.representation_reason: lens-geometry finding, §6.2: covering the leash-bounded worst-case spread (~4000uu diameter) requires CamFwd ~5500uu, at which individual billboards draw ~6-12px tall (illegible) regardless of headcount. Distance/coverage is the binding constraint, not body count — an aggregate block's on-screen size is a UI choice, not a 1/depth projection, so it never degrades.
army_view.fraction_note: 100% of squads represented, always — not a body-count fraction. Falls out of switching representation; nothing is ever dropped from frame because the leash radius bounds the required coverage to a known, fixed area.
army_view.sacrifices_first_note: Traded up front as a standing representation choice, not a per-frame crop. No cohesion-vs-bearer tradeoff applies here (see unit_squad_view for that).
army_view.block_sizing: standing / target-size-for-that-type (an understrength unit reads visibly smaller)
army_view.block_type_marker: 0.3 NEW — each block also carries a type label/icon (e.g. 'S·34' / 'A·12'), since blocks are no longer a single undifferentiated pool. Rendering detail, not a new representation; still O(max_squads) draws.
army_view.yaw: none — fixed top-down / bearer-heading-locked layout, does not use the perspective virtual camera or the yaw_envelope below

unit_squad_view.subject: the selected unit (see selection_responsiveness); falls back to the most-engaged unit if nothing is selected yet
unit_squad_view.representation: individual per-soldier billboards, same mechanism as today's close-up
unit_squad_view.note: Fraction is read against the SELECTED unit's standing count (corrected in 0.2 — the 0.1 draft's simulation table incorrectly computed fraction against whole-retinue count; see spec §6.1 of the prior revision). Body floor overrides the fraction at low counts. Unchanged in 0.3 — typed units don't change this view's math, only what a selected unit's own sprite looks like.

map_mode.purpose: the wider, on-demand 'more information and options' surface the owner asked for, and the actual answer to 'mini retinue units by default' (see army_view_lens_geometry.orthographic_check for why the compact panel can't be that answer).
map_mode.representation: real per-soldier positions, both types, orthographic top-down (fixed world-to-pixel scale, no camera pull-back math) — not the compact panel's aggregate blocks
map_mode.coverage: full leash-bound worst-case spread (4000uu diameter), same as army_view's coverage guarantee, achieved by scale not by camera distance
map_mode.recommended_panel_height_note: Interpolated from army_view_lens_geometry.orthographic_check's target-height table: 1200px lands sprites at ~18px tall and in-rank neighbor spacing at ~13px — workably legible. 1000px (15px sprites) is the floor; below that reproduces the compact panel's own illegibility.
map_mode.selection: clicking a unit cluster is the SAME selection action as a muster-card click / hotkey — see selection_responsiveness below
map_mode.leash_visualization: flagged as a natural fit (renders FLAME-FOUNDATION.md §3a's 'leash as lit floor', still unbuilt anywhere) — NOT specced or claimed solved here, a render-bridge task for whoever builds this mode
map_mode.cost_class: O(N) draw pass — same class as today's Unit/Squad View walk, cheaper per-unit if icons are flat primitives rather than atlas sprite frames. This is the first mode in this file's history to give up the O(max_squads) guarantee army_view/the old single-mode design had — see spec §8 performance requests.

selection_responsiveness.driver: same input as squad-addressed orders — muster card click or hotkey 1-8; selecting for command and for camera-viewing is the same action

transition.mode: travel (VInterpTo-based focus pull), not a hard cut
transition.speed_note: New dial, between ambient Emberkeep.UnitCamProj.FollowSpeed (6, ~0.5s settle) and Emberkeep.UnitCamProj.CastFocusSpeed (12, ~0.25s settle). At speed 10 a typical hop settles in ~0.3s. A hard cut across leash-radius distances (~2000uu) reads as a glitch; ambient FollowSpeed reads as unresponsive to a deliberate player action — this sits between the two on purpose.

persistence.mode_note: Selection holds until explicitly changed or cleared (same-card click / dedicated Army input toggles back). Recommended over idle-decay: a decay timer would yank the camera away during a deliberate sustained watch. Taste call, not technical — alternative below if playtesting disagrees.
persistence.idle_decay_alternative_note: Documented fallback dial, NOT the default. Only wire this in if the owner overrides the latch recommendation after playtesting.

selection_responsiveness.explicit_vs_auto_fallback: explicit selection always wins while active; the most-engaged-squad rule is only the fallback pick when Unit/Squad View is entered with nothing selected yet, and becomes a normal selection from that point (does not keep auto-following combat underneath it)
selection_responsiveness.selected_squad_wiped_mid_fight: drop to army_view (resting state) — do NOT auto-reselect a different squad the player never chose
selection_responsiveness.cast_focus_precedence: unchanged — cast-focus still outranks Army View, Unit/Squad View, and any selection; hands control back to whichever was active when the cast ends

primary_squad_selection_fallback.rule: the squad whose centroid has the most brood within CombatScan (default 1200uu) — the squad most engaged right now
primary_squad_selection_fallback.usage_note: Renamed from 0.1's 'primary_squad_selection' — this is now ONLY the fallback rule used when Unit/Squad View has no explicit player selection yet (see selection_responsiveness.explicit_vs_auto_fallback), not the camera's default subject.

yaw_envelope.scope: Unit/Squad View's virtual camera only — Army View does not use the perspective camera and has no yaw concept (see view_modes.army_view.yaw)
yaw_envelope.base_heading: bearer -> selected-squad-centroid direction (falls back to the bearer's last movement heading if no squad/centroid exists, e.g. retinue wiped)
yaw_envelope.look_lerp_note: Lowered from the current Emberkeep.UnitCamProj.LookLerp default of 3.0 — roughly doubles settle time so a swing across the full 60-degree arc reads as a deliberate pan, not a whip.
yaw_envelope.settle_note: Eases back to dead-on-base-heading whenever nothing inside CombatScan is pulling the auto-look, rather than holding wherever it last pointed.
yaw_envelope.cast_focus_override: unchanged — still punches through for its dialed duration (CastFocusSpeed/CastZoom)

army_view_lens_geometry.note: Supporting numbers for view_modes.army_view.representation_reason — see spec §6.2 for the full derivation. NOT measured against a real play session; qualitative conclusion (distance-bound, not count-bound) is robust, exact uu crossing points are estimates.
army_view_lens_geometry.area_saturation_note: Headcount-driven sprite overlap does not bind until ~6500+ bodies at the leash-covering distance — several multiples past any retinue size this repo has data for. Distance/coverage, not headcount, is what breaks individual-billboard legibility.

orthographic_check.status: NEW in 0.3 — spec §5.1, re-derives the above under an orthographic (fixed-scale) projection instead of perspective, to test whether projection method rescues per-soldier legibility for the owner's 'mini units by default' ask.
orthographic_check.finding: Matches the perspective numbers almost exactly (6.1/12.6 vs 6.08/12.55) — projection method does not change the binding constraint, which is panel_px * unit_size / world_diameter regardless of how that ratio is computed. Confirms the original 'distance/coverage, not headcount' finding generalizes to 'pixel budget, not projection method.'
orthographic_check.panel_height_needed_note: Solves panel_px = target_height * worst_case_spread_diameter_uu / sprite_world_height_uu (60uu = 2*UnitHalf(40)*SoldierScale(0.75)). This is what motivates map_mode's recommended_panel_height_px (1200) above — the compact panel (405-837px) cannot reach even the 10px row.

simulation_extrapolation.growth_rate_note: Placeholder net-growth-per-growth-site multiplier (+25%), standing in for 'recruit outweighs attrition when played competently' since no economy curve exists yet for a stage bigger than the 3-wave slice. NOT measured data.
simulation_extrapolation.single_pool_note: 0.2's finding, single undifferentiated pool — kept for reference. This is squad_manager.squad_size_legibility_ceiling (Unit/Squad View), not the Army View lens-geometry ceiling above — the two are independent findings.

typed_allocation_trajectory.status: NEW in 0.3 — spec §4.2, same growth assumptions extended to a two-pool split
typed_allocation_trajectory.finding: Breaks SOONER than the single-pool ~640-750 ceiling, and for a different reason: Spearmen alone consume the entire 8-unit budget once their own pool passes ~580 (ceil(580/80)=8), independent of Archers — at which point Archers are force-folded into one oversized unit regardless of how small the Archer pool is. Cross-type competition for the fixed 8-handle budget, not single-type growth, is the new binding constraint.
